title: cost-snapshotter-and-adaptive-quant-bundle-registrar
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight mechanism to capture a tenant-aware cost snapshot at decision points (model rollout, autoscale events, prefills) and to register compact quantization bundles that can be referenced by routing/policy rules. This PR introduces two cooperating subsystems: (1) Cost Snapshotter - a runtime hook that records short-lived unit-econ signals (per-tenant token mix, batch shapes, cache hit ratio, recently selected quant profile) to a compact, queryable store; (2) Quant Bundle Registrar - a small metadata service that validates, fingerprints, and publishes quantization bundles (quant configs + safety tags) to be used by the routing layer and Optimize recommendations.

What changed (high level):
- Cost Snapshotter: new runtime hook integrated into the request router; emits a compact protobuf to the snapshots store for sampling-enabled tenants. Snapshots are TTL'd and indexed by tenant, model, and request time-bucket.
- Snapshot ingestion pipeline: lightweight consumer that enriches snapshots with recent telemetry and persists derived unit-cost estimates to the cost-store used by the optimizer.
- Quant Bundle Registrar: CLI + HTTP endpoints to publish quant bundles, validate compatibility, and attach safety labels (loss-estimate, fallthrough-policy). Bundles are versioned and fingerprinted.
- Policy integration: routing policy logic extended to consult latest snapshot and registered bundle metadata when selecting model/quant variants for a request.
- Tests and docs: unit tests for the registrar, runtime smoke tests for snapshot emission, and an ops runbook for enabling sampling and bundle rollouts.

Design notes:
- Snapshots are intentionally compact (<= 1KB) and emitted at request-tail to avoid blocking.
- Registrar validates bundles by running a dry-run quant check on a small synthetic prompt set to approximate compatibility; expensive checks are gated behind a flag.
- By default sampling is off; rollout plan recommends enabling 1% tenant sampling then ramping.

Checklist:
- [x] Snapshot proto and migrations
- [x] Runtime hook + gated feature flag
- [x] Registrar API + CLI
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs: ops runbook + API docs

Backward compatibility: Registrations are additive. If routing cannot find a compatible registered bundle, it falls back to the existing quant selection logic.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy registrar in read-only mode and smoke test publishing CLI to staging.
2) Enable snapshot sampling for internal tenants (alice/dev) at 1%.
3) Validate cost estimates and ensure no perf regression under low sampling.
4) Gradually enable sampling on more tenants and flip on registrar-driven routing for canary tenants.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: extra write amplification on hot paths. Mitigation: snapshots are emitted asynchronously to an in-memory buffer with backpressure; when buffer is full we drop non-critical snapshots and record a metric.
- Risk: incorrect quant bundle causing quality regressions. Mitigation: safety labels and a staged rollout (dry-run compatibility checks + canary routing with automatic fallback).

Related: ENG-4238 (unit-econ hooks), SUP-1082 (customer report influencing sampling needs).
